prompt: Read the English sentence: 'Not all students failed the exam.' Does this mean: (a) No student passed, (b) At least one student passed, or (c) All students passed? Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
notes: Tests external negation of universal quantifier.

prompt: Read the English sentence: 'None of the students failed the exam.' Does this mean: (a) No student passed, (b) At least one student passed, or (c) All students passed? Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
notes: Minimal pair for en-neg-001a: negates an existential ('none of') rather than a universal ('not all'), so the correct reading flips from 'at least one passed' to 'all passed'. Isolates whether the model distinguishes ¬∃ from ¬∀ rather than pattern-matching negation+quantifier surface forms to a single default reading.

prompt: Read the English sentence: 'Not all of the buses were late.' Does this mean: (a) No bus was on time, (b) At least one bus was on time, or (c) All buses were on time? Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
notes: Second lexical instantiation of RULE_EN_NEG_SCOPE, using 'buses/late' instead of 'students/failed' so the category isn't validated on a single vocabulary item.

prompt: Read the English sentence: 'None of the buses were late.' Does this mean: (a) No bus was on time, (b) At least one bus was on time, or (c) All buses were on time? Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
notes: Second lexical instantiation of RULE_EN_NEG_UNIVERSAL_QUANT, paired with en-neg-002a.
